blocks.orig: Whether you’re visiting Tanzania in July, August, or even September, your summer holiday will be filled with unforgettable moments. Let’s explore what makes this the perfect time to visit, what the weather is like, and the unique activities you won’t want to miss.
blocks.html: Come to Tanzania in July, August or even September, and your summer holiday will be packed with moments you will never forget. Below we look at why this is such a good time to travel, what the weather does and which special activities you should not miss.

blocks.orig: What is the Weather Like in Tanzania in July and August?
blocks.html: How is the weather in Tanzania during July and August?

blocks.orig: If you’re wondering, “Is July a good time to visit Tanzania?“—definitely! And August is equally fantastic. The weather in Tanzania in July and August is cooler and drier, with temperatures ranging from 15°C to 25°C (59°F to 77°F). This pleasant climate is perfect for game drives, safaris, and other outdoor adventures. Say goodbye to the scorching heat—this is the ideal time to explore Tanzania in comfort!
blocks.html: Are you asking yourself, “Is July a good time to visit Tanzania?“—the answer is a clear yes! And August is every bit as good. The weather in Tanzania in July and August is cooler and drier, with the temperature sitting between 15°C and 25°C (59°F to 77°F). Such a pleasant climate suits game drives, safaris and any other outdoor adventure perfectly. No more sweltering heat—this is the time to discover Tanzania in comfort!

blocks.orig: Experience the allure of Tanzania during the months of July and August, a time when nature reveals its most breathtaking spectacles. This period is renowned for the Great Migration, where thousands of wildebeest and zebras embark on perilous river crossings in the Serengeti, creating an unforgettable wildlife drama.
blocks.html: Discover the appeal of Tanzania in July and August, the months when nature puts on its most dramatic show. This is the famous season of the Great Migration, when thousands of wildebeest and zebras brave dangerous river crossings in the Serengeti – wildlife drama you will never forget.

blocks.orig: With cooler temperatures enhancing your adventure, it’s the perfect opportunity to explore Tanzania’s stunning landscapes and vibrant ecosystems. After thrilling safari experiences, unwind on the idyllic beaches of Zanzibar, where relaxation and cultural exploration await.
blocks.html: The cooler temperatures make the adventure all the better, so it’s an ideal moment to discover Tanzania’s magnificent landscapes and lively ecosystems. Once the safari excitement is over, wind down on the dreamy beaches of Zanzibar, where rest and cultural discovery go hand in hand.

blocks.html: Whether you’re after close encounters with wildlife or quiet days on the beach, Tanzania in July and August gives you a rare mix of adventure and calm. So what exactly are the main reasons to visit Tanzania in summer?

blocks.orig: The Great Migration in Central and Northern Tanzania
blocks.html: The Great Migration in central and northern Tanzania

blocks.orig: From June to October, witness one of nature’s greatest spectacles—the river crossing of the Great Migration. This period is hence famous for the dramatic river crossings at the Mara River, where wildebeest and zebras risk it all as they move through Northern Tanzania’s Serengeti. Cooler temperatures during this time provide the best conditions for game drives and wildlife viewing. It’s truly one of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World!
blocks.html: Between June and October you can watch one of the greatest spectacles in nature—the river crossing of the Great Migration. This is the season known for the dramatic crossings of the Mara River, where wildebeest and zebras put everything on the line as they travel through Northern Tanzania’s Serengeti. The cooler weather at this time also creates the best conditions for game drives and watching wildlife. It really is one of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World!

blocks.orig: Unlike the hot, dry season earlier in the year, the cooler temperatures from June to September offer a refreshing climate, much like European summers. Whether you’re on a safari or taking part in outdoor excursions, the mild weather allows you to enjoy every moment. The cooler temperatures make it the perfect time to explore Tanzania’s national parks, and you’ll appreciate the comfortable climate while tracking wildlife 😉. Make sure to bring layers for your daily adventures so you are all set for “chillier” evenings during your safari or at the beach on Zanzibar. You don’t enjoy safaris in the steaming heat? Then this is your time to go on safari in Tanzania. The temperatures are cooler than usual so pack your sweater for cooler evenings and you are good to go!
blocks.html: In contrast to the hot, dry months earlier in the year, June to September brings cooler temperatures and a refreshing climate, not unlike a European summer. On safari or on an outdoor excursion, the mild weather lets you make the most of every moment. It is the ideal time to explore Tanzania’s national parks, and you will be glad of the comfortable climate while you track wildlife 😉. Do pack layers for your daily outings so you are prepared for “chillier” evenings on safari or on the beach in Zanzibar. Not a fan of safaris in sweltering heat? Then this is the moment to go on safari in Tanzania. Temperatures are lower than usual, so bring a sweater for the cooler evenings and you are all set!

blocks.orig: After the thrill of your safari, head to Zanzibar for some well-deserved relaxation. Sink your toes into the soft, powdery sands of Nungwi or Kendwa, take a refreshing dip in the crystal-clear waters, or explore the rich history and vibrant culture of Stone Town. Our favourite beach, Jambiani, will have you in wow throughout your whole vacation. We can definitely also recommend Paje as a beach relaxation destination! Zanzibar offers the perfect balance of relaxation and adventure, making it the ideal post-safari retreat.
blocks.html: Once the safari excitement is behind you, make your way to Zanzibar for some well-earned rest. Dig your toes into the soft, powdery sand at Nungwi or Kendwa, cool off in the crystal-clear sea or dive into the rich history and lively culture of Stone Town. Our favourite beach, Jambiani, will keep you in awe for your entire holiday. Paje is another beach we can warmly recommend for relaxing! With its ideal balance of relaxation and adventure, Zanzibar is the perfect place to retreat to after a safari.

blocks.orig: For a more intimate wildlife experience, take a walking safari in the Tarangire National Park, Manyara National Park or Arusha National Park (among many others). The cooler weather makes these treks even more enjoyable, as expert guides lead you through the wilderness, pointing out hidden details you might miss on a vehicle-based safari. This up-close experience allows you to connect with nature in a way few other activities can.
blocks.html: If you would like a more personal wildlife experience, join a walking safari in Tarangire National Park, Manyara National Park or Arusha National Park (to name just a few). The cooler weather makes these walks all the more pleasant, while expert guides take you through the bush and point out small details you would easily overlook from a vehicle. Few other activities let you connect with nature as closely as this.
